content.value_statement: NestJS architecture and debugging require careful module, provider, database, and authentication decisions. This skill guides diagnosis, implementation, review, and validation with established patterns.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses module imports, provider exports, circular dependencies, and injection token problems.
Guides controller validation, guards, interceptors, pipes, exception filters, and request lifecycle design.
Provides Jest, Supertest, repository mocking, integration testing, and end-to-end testing patterns.
Troubleshoots TypeORM, Mongoose, Prisma, database connections, entities, transactions, and query performance.
Reviews Passport, JWT, configuration, logging, caching, and production performance practices.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but cannot verify behavior without access to the target project.
Database, authentication, and deployment advice requires adaptation to local infrastructure and security requirements.
Referenced commands depend on scripts and packages already configured in the project.
Specialized TypeScript, database, Node.js runtime, and frontend issues may require another expert.

use_cases.title: Repair Dependency Injection
use_cases.description: Trace missing providers, exports, imports, scopes, and circular dependencies in a NestJS application.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developers maintaining an existing NestJS service

use_cases.title: Design a Tested Feature
use_cases.description: Plan modules, controllers, services, DTO validation, mocks, and end-to-end coverage for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess authentication, database handling, errors, logging, caching, performance, and test coverage before release.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a NestJS Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this NestJS error: [error]. Explain the likely cause, files to inspect, smallest fix, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner troubleshooting for a specific framework error

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Feature Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a NestJS module for [feature]. Include controllers, services, DTO validation, provider boundaries, error handling, and focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate feature design within an existing application

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NestJS architecture: [context]. Identify module boundary, dependency injection, database, authentication, testing, and performance risks. Prioritize concrete changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a service or pull request

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the migration from [current design] to [target design]. Preserve behavior, stage database changes, address security, and define rollback and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert planning for a high-risk architectural change

output_examples.input: Nest cannot resolve OrdersService in OrdersController.
output: Likely cause: OrdersService is missing from providers or is not exported by its owning module.
Inspect OrdersModule imports, providers, exports, and the controller constructor token.
Apply the smallest module metadata fix, then run build, unit tests, and relevant end-to-end tests.

output_examples.input: Review JWT authentication before production release.
output: Confirm one validated secret source is shared by JwtModule and JwtStrategy.
Check token expiry, bearer parsing, guard coverage, refresh handling, and configuration validation.
Add negative tests for missing, expired, malformed, and incorrectly signed tokens.

output_examples.input: A TypeORM application reports repeated connection failures.
output: Check entity decorator errors before treating the message as an infrastructure failure.
Verify connection names, entity registration, file paths, retry settings, and startup error handling.
Reproduce with one connection and validate each configuration change independently.

best_practices: Provide the exact error, relevant module metadata, framework version, and expected behavior.
Match existing project conventions and request the smallest change that resolves the confirmed cause.
Validate changes in order with build, unit, integration, and relevant end-to-end tests.
anti_patterns: Do not add broad module imports or forward references before confirming the dependency path.
Do not expose secrets, production tokens, or complete environment files in prompts.
Do not accept framework examples without adapting them to project versions and infrastructure.

faq.question: Which NestJS topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers modules, dependency injection, controllers, request lifecycle, testing, databases, authentication, configuration, errors, logging, caching, and performance.

faq.question: Can it modify my application?
faq.answer: It can guide or propose changes when project files are available. You should review changes and run the project test suite.

faq.question: Does it support TypeORM and Mongoose?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes configuration, entity or schema, repository, connection, testing, and performance guidance for both integrations.

faq.question: Can it help with JWT authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Passport strategies, guards, bearer tokens, secret configuration, token expiry, and authentication testing.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the error, NestJS version, relevant modules, providers, configuration, tests, and the behavior you expect.

faq.question: Does it replace project testing or security review?
faq.answer: No. Its guidance requires local validation, environment-specific testing, and additional review for sensitive production systems.
